title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
description: A sweeping story of justice, redemption, and love in nineteenth-century France as ex-convict Jean Valjean seeks a new life.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A practical handbook of agile software craftsmanship covering naming, functions, error handling, and clean refactoring.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: On the desert planet Arrakis, young Paul Atreides is drawn into a prophecy and a struggle over the galaxy's most precious resource.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins, a comfort-loving hobbit, joins thirteen dwarves and the wizard Gandalf on a quest to reclaim the Lonely Mountain.

title: The Design of Everyday Things
author: Don Norman
description: An essential primer on human-centered design, affordances, signifiers, and why intuitive products feel effortless to use.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: A deep exploration of the principles behind reliable, scalable, and maintainable distributed data systems.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas & Andrew Hunt
description: Timeless lessons on software engineering habits, orthogonality, tracer bullets, and taking ownership of your craft.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A lone astronaut wakes millions of miles from Earth with amnesia and must solve an extinction-level scientific mystery.

author: George Orwell
description: Winston Smith navigates life under the watchful gaze of Big Brother in a chilling portrait of surveillance and truth.

title: The Name of the Wind
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: Kvothe recounts his journey from a troupe of traveling players to an orphan survivor and legendary student at the University.

title: Refactoring UI
author: Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger
description: Actionable visual design tactics for developers covering hierarchy, spacing, color systems, and typography without guesswork.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: A lone human envoy travels to the frozen world of Gethen to bridge cultures and confront profound questions of identity.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: In St. Petersburg, impoverished student Raskolnikov wrestles with guilt, morality, and redemption after a fateful act.

title: The Elements of Typographic Style
author: Robert Bringhurst
description: A celebrated classic on rhythm, proportion, page harmony, and the craft of choosing and setting type.
